whyNutype.heading: Built by design
whyNutype.paragraph:
I'm Dan, and I've spent over fifteen years in branding, advertising and motion design before starting Nutype. That means every project gets senior-level thinking and hands-on craft.

I work best with businesses that have a genuinely good story to tell but aren't landing it: logistics firms, law and accountancy practices, charities, specialist retailers like toy & games shops or products that need to stand out. If that sounds like you, we'll probably get on well.

No bloated process, no handing your project between five different people. Branding, campaigns and motion, all under one roof, built around what actually works for your audience rather than what's trending this week.

legalPages.title: AI Policy
legalPages.body:
**1. Purpose**

I use AI tools to work faster and smarter, not to replace the thinking, taste and relationships that make Nutype Creative what it is. This policy sets out honestly how I use AI, where I draw the line, and how I protect your information.

**2. What I will use AI for**

- Research, early brainstorming and first drafts, to speed up the start of a project.
- Repetitive or admin tasks: scheduling, basic admin, first-pass proofreading, resizing and formatting files.
- Rough concepts or reference material, which I then develop, refine and finish myself.
- Initial outreach and onboarding messages. Once we're working together, our communication stays human.

**3. What I will NOT use AI for**

- Setting your final pricing or agreeing contract terms. That decision is always mine.
- Responding to sensitive client complaints or difficult conversations. I handle these personally.
- Final logo and brand identity decisions, and quality checks before anything is delivered to you.
- Giving copyright or legal advice, or anything that could put your business or mine at risk.
- Building our relationship. AI can help draft an email, but once we're working together, it's me you're dealing with.

**4. Data and privacy**

I treat your information like I'd want mine treated. I never put client contact details, passwords, login details, contracts, NDAs, pricing agreements or private financial information into AI tools. I never share commercially sensitive creative, branding, campaign work without your permission.

If I do need AI's help with something you've shared (for example, checking a layout that includes an address), I remove or anonymise identifying details first wherever I can, use private or incognito chat sessions, and delete files from AI tools once I'm finished with them.

I use AI tools with training switched off wherever that option exists, so what I input isn't used to train their models.

If I ever put something into an AI tool by mistake that shouldn't be there, I'll tell you and do everything I can to remove it.

No AI tool is completely secure, so sensitive material stays out of them altogether rather than relying on a provider's settings or promises.

**5. Human review**

Everything AI touches is checked by me before it reaches you, including making sure AI-assisted visuals don't copy someone else's copyrighted work or style. AI can be confidently wrong, and it doesn't understand your brand, your customers or your business the way I do. I'm the final set of eyes on every piece of work, every time.

**6. Transparency with clients**

If AI has played a meaningful part in a piece of work, I'll tell you. You're always welcome to ask how much of something was AI-assisted, and I'll give you a straight answer.

**7. Review and updates**

AI tools and best practice are moving quickly, and I'm currently a one-person studio, so I won't pretend this policy is fixed forever. As the studio grows, this policy will extend to cover any freelancers or subcontractors working with me, and I'll let you know when that happens. I'll review it at least once a year, or sooner if something important changes.
